chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu al-'Atarid said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I buy food, I place [a specific amount] at the beginning, and I profit at the end, so I ask my partner to deduct from me such and such for every kur [measure].' He said: 'There is no good in this, but he should deduct a lump sum from you.' I said: 'If he deducts from me more than what I placed [initially]?' He said: 'There is no harm.' I said: 'So I take out the kur and the two kurs, and the man says to me: Give it to me for your measure.' He said: 'If he trusts you, there is no harm.'

key_terms.اِئْتَمَنَكَ: If he trusts you / in a trust-based arrangement
key_terms.كُرٍّ: A unit of volume/measure for grain

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on partnership trade where one partner deducts more than their initial contribution?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of variable profit-sharing in trade partnerships, distinguishing between fixed deductions per unit and lump-sum adjustments. The Imam validates exceeding the initial contribution if based on mutual trust (*i'timan*), reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on flexibility in commercial contracts (*mu'amalat*) provided there is no deception (*gharar*). This highlights the practical application of trust as a foundational element in Islamic economic ethics.
